summary: Published src/content/blog/beginner/short-head-line-meaning.md, a beginner companion article for the Short Head Line Meaning Next 25 backlog item. The article grounds the core meaning in the already-established repository reading (Benham and Gettings: a shorter head line indicates a focused, direct, efficient mental approach, not limited intelligence), sourced from src/content/lessons/lines/03-head-line.mdx and the already-published src/content/blog/beginner/head-line.md. Added a reciprocal internal link from head-line.md's Length section to the new article, and updated docs/editorial-backlog.md's published count (62 -> 63) and cross-link tracking table.

source_preflight.notes: All 8 claim-risk PREVALENCE_OR_CONSENSUS flags manually dispositioned: the 'most frequently distorts' / 'most commonly distorted' language paraphrases the lesson's own stated claim (03-head-line.mdx: 'the reading that popular palmistry most frequently distorts'); 'generally treated as short' and 'rarely the most decisive on its own' are Palmistry Path's own editorial/observational conventions (mirroring the already-published short-heart-line-meaning.md pattern), not attributed traditional-source claims; remaining flags ('most alarming', 'ranging widely across many') are reader-framing or idiomatic phrasing, not palmistry prevalence claims. Only two quoted phrases are used ('abundant mentality', 'kind to be estimated by the character and color of the line'), both taken verbatim from the already-verified Benham quotation in head-line.md (confirmed against docs/source-verification-log.md line 409). No Gettings/Cheiro/West/Fincham quotes were fabricated -- Gettings' framing is paraphrased only, per the lesson, since Gettings quotations are flagged unverifiable (copyright-era) in docs/editorial-backlog.md. No new combination reading was introduced: the 'Length in context' section explicitly states approved sources do not set out a combined short-length + endpoint/slope/hand-shape reading and does not assert one. The article repeatedly and explicitly rejects the short=low-intelligence / IQ inference rather than asserting it, and makes no medical, legal, financial, or predictive-science claim.
